items.title: Brent crude hits $141 as Hormuz closure fuels worst energy crisis since 1970s

featured_image.name: Brent oil price for actual cargo soars to $141, highest ...

items.description:
More than five weeks after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran, the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz has plunged global energy markets into their worst crisis since the 1970s, with Brent crude surging past $112 per barrel and governments worldwide scrambling to shield their economies from deepening fuel shortages.

The war began on February 28, 2026, when U.S. and Israeli forces conducted nearly 900 strikes in 12 hours targeting Iranian military infrastructure and leadership, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Iran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the Middle East, including strikes on oil infrastructure and vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of the world's oil supply normally passes. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps formally declared the strait closed to vessels traveling to or from the U.S., Israel, and their allies on March 27.[1][2]

items.title: Trump claims Iran military leaders 'terminated' in Tehran strike

featured_image.name: Trump: U.S. will bomb Iran "back to stone ages" over next 2-3 weeks

items.description:
President Trump escalated his rhetoric against Iran on Saturday, warning that Tehran has 48 hours to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or reach a peace deal before the United States unleashes "all hell" on the country. The ultimatum, posted on Truth Social, sets a deadline of Monday, April 6, as the war enters its sixth week with no end in sight.[1][2][3]

"Remember when I gave Iran ten days to MAKE A DEAL or OPEN UP THE HORMUZ STRAIT," Trump wrote. "Time is running out — 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them. Glory be to GOD!" It marks the second time Trump has issued such a deadline; a similar 48-hour ultimatum on March 21 was eventually postponed after what Trump described as "good and productive" peace talks — claims Iranian state media denied.[4][5][6][1]

items.title: Iran threatens 'crushing' strikes on US, Israeli assets across Middle East

items.description: Iran's armed forces on Saturday issued their most sweeping threat yet in the five-week-old war, warning that any further US strikes on Iranian infrastructure would be met with "sustained and destructive" attacks on all American and Israeli assets across the Middle East. The escalation came as Tehran rejected a US-backed 48-hour ceasefire proposal, leaving diplomatic efforts in disarray.

items.title: US-Israeli jets strike Tehran's Shahid Beheshti University

featured_image.name: US-Israeli Airstrikes Target Shahid Beheshti University in ...

items.description: American and Israeli fighter jets struck Shahid Beheshti University in Tehran on Friday, destroying a research facility and a women's dormitory at one of Iran's leading academic institutions, according to Iranian state media. The attack marks the latest escalation in a campaign that has now damaged universities, hospitals, and research centers across the country, drawing a sharp rebuke from more than 100 international law experts who warn the strikes may constitute war crimes.
